Beyond code coverage, how can I evaluate whether my test suite is good at detecting faults?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
I now have comprehensive SWEBOK coverage across all the relevant dimensions. Here is the synthesized list of guidelines.

---

## Guidelines for Evaluating Test Suite Fault-Detection Effectiveness Beyond Code Coverage

---

### 1. Use Fault Injection to Measure How Many Seeded Faults Your Tests Reveal

Artificially introduce known faults into the system under test (SUT) before running your suite. The proportion of injected faults discovered tells you how effectively the suite detects defects, and can be used to estimate the number of genuine faults still present.

> "[SWEBOK excerpt b98a01ab11a6bb389235]."

(source: `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/Mutation Testing and Fault Injection Evaluation.md`)

> **Caveat:** Apply this technique with care—statisticians question how representative injected faults are of real ones, and there is the risk of leaving seeded faults in the SUT. (source: same file)

---

### 2. Compute the Mutation Score to Quantify Test Suite Strength

Apply mutation testing: generate many slightly modified versions (mutants) of the SUT, run your test suite against each one, and measure what fraction of mutants it "kills." A higher mutation score signals stronger fault-detection ability.

> "[SWEBOK excerpt c55903435d9db2cf30b2]."

(source: `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/Mutation Testing and Fault Injection Evaluation.md`)

> "[SWEBOK excerpt c027aef58b4a93d21946] … [SWEBOK excerpt c5e3b75bef6ab3cf87a7] … [SWEBOK excerpt 54911efd10da1534ecc2] [SWEBOK excerpt 92398cd5ba1475bae1f8]."

(source: `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/Fault Models and Mutation Testing Techniques.md`)

---

### 3. Write New Tests Specifically Targeting Surviving Mutants

Do not stop at measuring the score passively. When mutants survive (are not killed), design new test cases specifically to kill them. This actively closes gaps in fault-detection ability.

> "[SWEBOK excerpt c09e66ee0e34e64a251b]."

(source: `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/Mutation-Based and Usage-Based Testing Techniques/Mutation Testing as a Testing Criterion.md`)

---

### 4. Apply Fault-Based Testing Using a Fault Model or Defect Classification

Use a fault model or taxonomy (such as Orthogonal Defect Classification) to systematically identify which categories of faults are most likely in your SUT, and verify that your test suite specifically targets those [SWEBOK excerpt 5ffde2fa1ef61341f4e9]. … a variety of platforms and development processes … [SWEBOK excerpt 19cfa87a5165e08cc5f0]."

(source: `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/Fault Models and Mutation Testing Techniques.md`)

> "[SWEBOK excerpt 860d2453eaf6e85c9e45]."

(source: `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Testing Approaches and Execution Strategies/Smoke Testing and Knowledge-Based Testing Approaches.md`)

---

### 5. Leverage Fault Type History and Statistics to Focus the Suite

Examine records from earlier projects to understand which fault types occur most frequently in your domain. Use this empirical knowledge to verify that the test suite addresses high-frequency fault categories.

> "[SWEBOK excerpt 4bc5372472a04a0e0f08]."

(source: `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/SUT Measurements and Fault Classification for Test Planning.md`)

---

### 6. Use Error Guessing Informed by Domain Expertise and Fault History

Complement systematic techniques with error guessing: have experienced testers design cases targeting the most plausible faults, drawing on historical fault data and their own knowledge of the SUT.

> "[SWEBOK excerpt 58750920721c36886ebb]."

(source: `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Testing Approaches and Execution Strategies/Software Testing Techniques and Methodologies/Experience-Based Techniques for Test Suite Generation.md`)

---

### 7. Combine Specification-Based and Structure-Based Techniques

Evaluate whether your suite was produced using multiple complementary techniques. Because specification-based (black-box) and structure-based (white-box) approaches expose different kinds of faults, using both together improves overall fault-detection coverage.

> "[SWEBOK excerpt 5957a5d79fa90b756cf0]."

(source: `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/Testing Approaches and Test Case Selection Methods/Combining Functional and Structural Testing Techniques.md`)

> "[SWEBOK excerpt aea5439e172ef2f8a26e]."

(source: `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/Testing Methods and System Diversity/Software Testing Techniques and Standards.md`)

---

### 8. Apply Reliability Growth Models to Assess Remaining Fault Exposure

Track failures over time and fit reliability growth models to the data. If the failure rate is not decreasing (the model is not "growing"), the suite may not be exercising fault-prone areas effectively; conversely, a levelling-off can support a stop-testing decision.

> "[SWEBOK excerpt 5d8c08207647395b407d] … the product's reliability will increase."

(source: `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/Reliability Growth Models and Test Evaluation.md`)

> "[SWEBOK excerpt 8893c561da18cf7b3381]."

(source: `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Assurance and Defect Management/Quality Metrics, Reliability Models, and Corrective Actions/Software Quality Measurements and Reliability Models.md`)

---

### 9. Measure Relative Effectiveness by Comparing Techniques Empirically

Do not evaluate a test suite in isolation. Use empirical comparisons—such as the ratio of faults found through testing versus total faults found during and after testing, or [SWEBOK excerpt 28ceef9587ac997f4a32]—to benchmark the suite against alternative techniques or historical baselines.

> "[SWEBOK excerpt c4ad890b5668c6dfc1ec]."

(source: `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/Test Effectiveness and Process Levels/Test Suite Effectiveness and Testing Process Integration.md`)

---

### 10. Use Operational Profiles to Evaluate Fault Detection Relative to Real-World Usage

Assess whether the test suite exercises the SUT in proportion to how it will actually be used. Faults in high-frequency usage paths matter most; a suite that ignores them cannot be called effective regardless of its other metrics.

> "[SWEBOK excerpt 5146d0173f4dd60f4661])."

(source: `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Testing Methodologies and Quality Assurance Practices/Software Testing Techniques, Measurement, and Management/Operational Profile Testing for Software Reliability.md`)

---

### 11. Use Injection-Based Tools to Confirm SUT Behavior Under Known Fault Conditions

Beyond manually seeding faults, employ dedicated injection-based tools to systematically reproduce known problem conditions and confirm the suite detects them reliably.

> "Injection-based tools … [SWEBOK excerpt 0d7260210eb931d71dfa]."

(source: `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Testing Tools and Standards/Software Testing Tools and Techniques/Software Testing and Reliability Evaluation Tools.md`)

---

**What the SWEBOK does not explicitly cover** in the passages retrieved: quantitative thresholds for an "acceptable" mutation score, specific guidance on how large a mutant population is sufficient, or automated oracle strategies for assessing test suite correctness in AI/ML systems—those topics are only mentioned briefly and without prescriptive guidance in the passages found.
